title: Replacement of the Central Maintenance Computer Rack and Flight Deck Display
abstract: A wider rack, a data concentrator and a higher resolution flight deck display replace the initial maintenance system installation, giving room for the correlation functions that the earlier rack could not host.

sections.reason: The initial display standard solved the access problem but left the maintenance system unable to correlate faults across systems, because there was no processing behind the screen and the rack had no spare slot. Operators who had taken the initial standard reported that the screen was little more than a fixed window on the same fault list. The obsolescence of the original display backlight, notified in 2021, made a like-for-like replacement unattractive and the two drivers were combined into one change.
sections.description: The rack KEDE588674-53 is replaced by a wider unit with two spare slots, and a data concentrator KAD366597-92 is installed in one of them to host the cross-system fault correlation. The flight deck display D4520115601387 is replaced by a higher resolution unit in the same aperture. The maintenance antenna 72TN is retained. The terminal control panel 169TN8 gains a correlation menu and the terminal computer 6796TN8 is re-cabled to the concentrator. Work is in zones 241 and 116, with the avionics rack area opened. Aircraft that never took the initial display standard need the flight deck aperture cut, which is why the modification is conditional on that earlier standard being present.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 6.4 kg per aircraft over the initial standard. Electrical load increase of 180 VA. Not interchangeable: the concentrator will not fit the narrow rack and the new display will not drive from the old bus. Fault correlation removes an estimated one in five no-fault-found removals according to the in-service data used in the business case. Maintenance system interrogation tasks require reissue throughout the documentation set.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in at MSN M00419 in March 2024. Retrofit through Service Bulletin MRD-45-1021, applicable only to aircraft already at the initial display standard, and taking two shifts with two people. Aircraft without that standard need a separate quotation because of the flight deck panel work.

type_data.balance_impact: Forward of the datum, CG shift below 0.03 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN M00419, avionics rack loom change in the forward fuselage build
